newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka hunts for illegal guns before polls.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka hunts for illegal guns before polls.

text.p: Sri Lankan police have launched a nationwide crackdown on unlicensed guns to curb political violence before next month's local elections, police said on Tuesday.
Those found guilty of possessing firearms illegally could face the death penalty, the defence ministry has said.
More than 1,000 police and soldiers have conducted raids on firearms suspects, Mohammed Nizam, deputy inspector-general of the police crimes branch told Reuters.

The crackdown came after the government of President Chandrika Kumaratunga announced last week it planned to tighten laws to bring gun-carrying political activists to justice before next month's local government elections.

Sri Lanka's gun culture became a key public issue after a young People's Alliance member of parliament was gunned down earlier this month during a roadside quarrel between supporters of the ruling alliance and those of the main opposition United National Party.
"We have already taken into custody a number of unauthorised firearms and several people who had them in their possession," Nizam said.
"Upon hearing this, people have voluntarily surrendered a large number of unauthorised firearms," he added.
State radio said on Tuesday that the government had granted an amnesty until March 4 for the surrender of illegal weapons.
The defence ministry said on Monday that anybody found possessing guns, explosives or an offensive weapon without lawful authority could face the death penalty or a jail term of up to 20 years.

Politicians and political activists in Sri Lanka own a large number of guns, many of them unlicensed, to guard themselves against possible attack by Tamil rebels who are fighting a separatist war in the island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year.
"This culture of violence and assassinations has to end. We welcome the new initiatives by police to take back the guns," said ruling People's Alliance (PA) lawmaker Jagath Balasuriya.

Police said 17 suspects were in custody for the killing of MP Nalanda Ellawala in Kuruwita, 80 km (50 miles) south of Colombo, on February 11. Among the suspects were UNP lawmaker Susantha Punchinilame and Mahinda Ratnatilleke, a former UNP mayor.
The killing came a day before nominations closed for the March 21 polls, seen as the first test of popularity for the PA since it came to power in 1994.
